# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Title: Stress-regulated phosphorylation of a GLFG FG-nucleoporin (lead candidate Nup98) impairs karyopherin docking, initiating selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In sporadic ALS motor neurons carrying TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained stress activates a kinase that phosphorylates clustered Ser/Thr residues in or near the GLFG repeats of an FG-nucleoporin — lead candidate Nup98, benchmarked against Nup153, Nup50, and Nup62. The initiating lesion is reduced karyopherin (TNPO1/importin-β) docking at phosphorylated FG repeats, causing selective failure of facilitated import before TDP-43 egress; altered passive permeability is a separately measured secondary attribute, not part of the initiation claim. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing (S3), stress-granule (SG) sequestration of transport factors (S4), Ran collapse, and cell death are downstream amplifiers. C9orf72 disease (S2) is out of scope.

Supported premises (packet only). S1: nuclear-pore/transport disruption co-occurs with TDP-43 pathology in ALS tissue and experimental systems — co-occurrence without direction. S3: SG-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and mislocalize transport proteins — the downstream arm. S4: SG assembly sequesters transport factors and impairs transport — both a sequestration alternative and the ground for predicting partial, graded phospho-null protection. S2: transport dysfunction only in the C9 genetic context, justifying the excluded scope.

Assumptions (no packet support). A1: a stress-activated kinase (p38/JNK candidates) phosphorylates FG-nucleoporins in adult motor neurons. A2: residue nominations rest on mitotic phospho-mapping analogy (unverified prior knowledge), used only after MS confirmation. A3: phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress — inverted from S1's co-occurrence. A4: restriction to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. A5 (declared biophysical bridge): GLFG phosphorylation lowers TNPO1/importin binding affinity, hence facilitated import, and secondarily alters passive permeability; A5 gates the program.

Target nomination replaces a priori choice. Phase 0: comparative site-level phospho-proteomics (TMT/SILAC MS) of enriched nuclear envelopes from stressed human motor neurons across a stress time course, screening Nup98, Nup62, Nup153, Nup50, and Nup214. Rule: advance the nucleoporin whose pore-localized phospho-occupancy rises before detectable import decline; Nup98 proceeds only if it passes. The resulting full site map then bounds the compensatory-phosphorylation search space in all later tests.

Causal chain. Kinase activation → FG/GLFG phosphorylation → reduced karyopherin docking (A5) → selective facilitated-import failure. 'Selective' is tested, not asserted: TNPO1-dependent PY-NLS cargos (hnRNPA1 reporter; fluorescent TDP-43 PY-NLS and full-length TDP-43) should decline preferentially versus generic importin-α/β NLS cargo, with passive dextran flux quantified separately. Downstream: nuclear TDP-43 loss → de-mixing (S3) → SG sequestration (S4) → Ran collapse → death; Ran is a downstream readout only.

Alternative explanations. (1) Sequestration-first: SGs or TDP-43 assemblies deplete soluble import machinery; phosphorylation irrelevant. (2) Physical pore displacement by insoluble TDP-43 (S1-consistent); phosphorylation a bystander. (3) C9orf72 route (S2). (4) Late phosphorylation secondary to stress.

Discriminating strategy.
- A5 gate: recombinant FG-domain construct of the mapped target phosphorylated in vitro with the mapped kinase (stoichiometry QC by intact mass plus targeted-site MS), plus matched phospho-null (Ser→Ala). Measure TNPO1 and importin-α/β binding (SPR or anisotropy); in digitonin-permeabilized neurons, measure passive flux and facilitated import kinetics as separately attributed outcomes. Proceed downstream only if phosphorylation reduces karyopherin binding and facilitated import.
- Temporal tests: pore-resolved time course of phospho-occupancy, TNPO1-cargo import, and TDP-43 localization; pulse–washout is supportive only.
- Perturbational test: CRISPR phospho-null panel at MS-verified sites, interpreted only after MS-verified occupancy suppression across the full site map; metric is TNPO1-cargo import decline normalized to SG burden and soluble import-factor availability. Prediction: phospho-null attenuates the early normalized decline versus wild type at matched SG burden — partial, since S4 impairment is phosphorylation-independent; late-phase failure is non-discriminating.
- In vivo work is staged only after in vitro discrimination; post-mortem phospho-staining of inclusion-free neurons is corroboration only.

Falsifying observations — each alone sufficient. (F1) With MS-verified suppression of the targeted phospho-cluster and no compensating elevation at any site detected in that nucleoporin's full MS map, mild stress yields an early-phase normalized TNPO1-cargo import decline indistinguishable from wild type at matched SG burden and soluble import-factor levels: a nil phosphorylation-attributable component under causally verified suppression makes phosphorylation non-necessary for initiation. (F2) Detectable TNPO1-cargo import failure precedes any measurable pore phospho-signal above validated reagent threshold. Non-decisive by rule: import failure persisting after phospho-loss in washout is equally predicted by self-sustaining downstream lesions within an initiating model, so it is supportive only; phosphomimetic outcomes carry no evidentiary weight in either direction.

Limitations. Scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS; kinase, residues, and direction remain assumptions pending MS; phosphorylation sites below MS detection are unbounded; Asp/Glu mimicry is weak and secondary only; iPSC and mouse models may not reproduce decades-long onset; post-mortem tissue is late-stage; phospho-signals are transient.

Ranked proposal:
Stress-regulated phosphorylation of a GLFG FG-nucleoporin (lead candidate Nup98) impairs karyopherin docking, initiating selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons
